known.title: The user choice to drop the allowBuilds deny without a trustedDependencies field rests on a false premise: Bun trusts @anthropic-ai/claude-code by default, so its postinstall runs on every install and the deny-by-default rule breaks.
known.locator: Research, Decisions, entry 3 (line 46); Steps, bun_lockfile_policy row (line 70)
known.summary: User: the plan records that the user chose to drop the allowBuilds deny and add no trustedDependencies field because 'Bun runs no dependency lifecycle script unless the project trusts the package' (citing https://bun.com/docs/pm/lifecycle). The cited page says the opposite: Bun runs lifecycle scripts for packages on an allow list, a curated list of popular npm packages is allowed by default, and its table states that omitting trustedDependencies trusts the built-in list, while only `trustedDependencies: []` trusts nothing. The built-in list linked from that page holds @anthropic-ai/claude-code (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.0/src/install/default-trusted-dependencies.txt, line 2). Scenario: after step bun_lockfile_policy, every `bun install --frozen-lockfile` (locally, in the three ci.yml jobs and in dependency-integrity.yml) runs claude-code's postinstall and materializes the ~230MB binary that pnpm-workspace.yaml:3-7 denies today. That breaks the constraint at .github/AGENTS.md:106 (deny-by-default lifecycle scripts for claude-code) and the note at .github/AGENTS.md:107 that the explicit install.cjs step materializes the binary the install skips; .github/AGENTS.md:100 says not to undo a mitigation to simplify a diff. Fix: correct the premise, set `"trustedDependencies": []` in package.json in step bun_lockfile_policy, keep the install.cjs step, rewrite .github/AGENTS.md:106 for trustedDependencies, and add an Acceptance row such as `node -p "JSON.stringify(require('./package.json').trustedDependencies)"` printing `[]`.

known.title: Acceptance A11 claims to prove the Bun install cache keyed on bun.lock, but it only counts actions/cache uses, which are already 3 at the snapshot, so it cannot fail.
known.summary: The Goal requires that the repository caches with Bun 1.4 instead of pnpm, and step workflow_contracts moves each cache step to ~/.bun/install/cache under a key that hashes bun.lock and package.json. A11 runs `grep -c 'uses: actions/cache@' .github/workflows/ci.yml` and expects `3`. At the snapshot, ci.yml already has exactly three `uses: actions/cache@55cc8345... # v6.1.0` lines (.github/workflows/ci.yml:118, :185, :260), all keyed on hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'package.json'). So A11 prints 3 before and after the change, and it passes with a cache still keyed on pnpm-lock.yaml, on a deleted lockfile, or on ~/.pnpm-store. No other row checks the cache: A9 only proves no pnpm text, A10 only the setup-bun pin, and A13 is a regression gate that passes before the change too. Fix: replace A11 with a row that fails without the change, for example `grep -c "hashFiles('bun.lock', 'package.json')" .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/dependency-integrity.yml` expecting ci.yml:3 and dependency-integrity.yml:1, plus a check that each cache path is ~/.bun/install/cache.

known.title: Research claims that the release tool refuses a branch other than main, but scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs:271 only checks for a clean tree, so step release_plan_lifecycle can release from a stale or non-main checkout.
known.locator: Research, Facts, Release flow (line 27); Steps, release_plan_lifecycle row (line 69)
known.summary: The Release flow fact says runGenericPluginRelease 'refuses a dirty working tree or a branch other than main before it bumps anything (scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs:271)', and step release_plan_lifecycle relies on it: it runs `node scripts/release.mjs --plugin plan-lifecycle 0.5.0` 'in the current checkout' because 'the branch check of the release tool keeps the bump on main'. At the snapshot, :271 is `if (!dryRun && !io.ensureCleanTree()) throw ...`, ensureCleanTree (:415-417) only tests `git status --porcelain`, and runGenericPluginRelease (:256-368) has no branch check at all; push() runs `git push origin HEAD` (:428-430) and createTag tags HEAD (:409-413). Scenario: step merge_cutover merges pull request #11 on GitHub, so a local main is stale. On the stale main, the tool commits the bump on the pre-merge commit and the push is rejected after the local commit; on any other branch, it pushes that branch, tags a non-main commit, passes tag CI and publishes the GitHub release from bytes that are not main. The Goal 'released from main' fails. Fix: correct the fact, and make step release_plan_lifecycle run `git switch main` and `git pull --ff-only origin main` (or verify `git rev-parse HEAD` equals `origin/main`) before the gate and the release, and check in Done when that the tag commit is on main.

No instruction file or contract rule requires a major bump for a breaking change, and the PR's BREAKING CHANGE footer is real (https://github.com/DocksDocks/docks/pull/11).

User: the user chose to adopt Bun 1.4.0 on its release day, 2026-08-20, with an exact pin, the full gate and a git revert path as mitigations, although the repository quarantines fresh npm versions for three days. Sound: Bun 1.4.0 was published on 2026-08-20 (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.4.0, published_at 2026-08-20T14:07:21Z; https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4 dated 2026-08-20). The quarantine (pnpm-workspace.yaml:2, ported as minimumReleaseAge) filters npm package versions during installation (https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/install, Minimum release age), not the Bun executable that setup-bun installs; .github/AGENTS.md:106's 'bump it only to a version aged past the quarantine' is about the claude-code devDependency. The plan keeps every supply-chain mitigation it touches except the separate decision 3 (SHA-pinned setup-bun per .github/AGENTS.md:103, actions/cache per :105, age gate ported, npm audit signatures per :108). The exact pin bun@1.4.0 is what setup-bun reads from packageManager (https://github.com/oven-sh/setup-bun#readme). The choice is the user's explicit risk acceptance, recorded with mitigations, and breaks no instruction file or contract rule.

Request correction: asked that 'Bun installs, caches and runs every gate', the plan makes Bun the installer, cache and starter of every package script and tool binary that pnpm started, while each gate script keeps running on Node 24 (`node scripts/ci.mjs` stays the entry point; package.json:6-17 scripts call node or biome). Sound: AGENTS.md:10 pins Node 24 to match CI's node-version (.github/workflows/ci.yml:38-41 and the other setup-node steps, asserted at scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs:2127-2129); scripts/AGENTS.md:3 states all tooling is Node .mjs; pnpm was never the runtime, so replacing pnpm means Bun takes the package-manager role; `bun run` runs scripts in a subshell and keeps a node-shebang CLI on Node unless --bun (https://bun.com/docs/runtime); Bun 1.4 states it is not 100% compatible with Node.js yet (https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4, Node.js compatibility). Steps gate_subprocesses and workflow_contracts carry it out, and Do not touch keeps the Node 24 runtime. No instruction file asks for a Bun runtime, and the Goal sentence ('runs its package scripts with Bun') matches what the steps do.
